result.summary: Re-gate limited to the S5 rework (commit 15b6ec2, at HEAD 201a931) that closes my prior FAIL (handoffs/WF02-REQ-018/step-02c-security-reviewer.json): requireEventStaffForEvent wrote no AuditLog row on any /checkin authorization refusal. Not a full re-run of S1-S14 against the whole requirement (already PASSed there); scoped to what changed since. 1. Read git show 15b6ec2 myself in full. It touches exactly apps/bot/src/domain/auditLog.ts (actorUserId: string -> string | null), apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts (new pure buildCheckinRefusalAudit(user, eventId, reason) plus a single writeAuditLog call added inside requireEventStaffForEvent, on every !result.ok branch, never on ok=true), apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.test.ts (4 new unit cases), and its own handoff bookkeeping file. Confirmed via `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-018 --name-only` that the full requirement diff still contains no other files beyond what I already passed in my original S1-S14 run plus this rework set (domain/eventStaff.ts+test, domain/user.ts, handlers/staff.ts, handlers/checkin.ts [unchanged by the rework itself], i18n/*, index.ts, docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md, handoffs/*) -- nothing outside apps/bot/** or handoff bookkeeping. handlers/checkin.ts itself has zero lines changed in 15b6ec2 -- the fix lives entirely in the domain layer, confirmed by reading the commit diff directly rather than trusting the commit message's claim. 2. Did NOT trust REVIEWER's re-gate report (step-02b-reviewer-regate.json) despite it already live-verifying all three branches -- re-derived myself, independently, against a fresh scratch Postgres I stood up myself (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432, `docker compose up -d`, `npx drizzle-kit migrate` against DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot; migrations applied cleanly, 4 files in apps/bot/drizzle/). Built the bot (`npm run build -w apps/bot`, tsc clean). Wrote a throwaway script (apps/bot/verify_regate.mjs, not committed -- deleted after use, confirmed by `git status --porcelain` returning empty before finishing) that constructs a real grammY Bot wired to the compiled makeCheckInHandler(db) with a stubbed sendMessage API transformer (no real Telegram token/network), seeds a real chapter + one not-yet-ended published event, and dispatches real bot.handleUpdate() calls with a correctly-formed bot_command entity. Counted audit_log rows before/after myself: - 'no-user' branch (tg_id with no User row at all): before=0, after=1, delta=+1. Row: {actorUserId: null, action: 'checkin.refused', entity: 'event', entityId: , payload: {reason: 'no-user'}}. - 'not-staff-for-event' branch (a registered member user, no event_staff row for this event) -- S5's own named negative case ('scanner is not staff'): before=1, after=2 cumulative (delta=+1 for this branch alone, isolated by re-counting immediately before/after the second dispatch). Row: {actorUserId: , action: 'checkin.refused', entity: 'event', entityId: , payload: {reason: 'not-staff-for-event'}}. Both: exactly +1, never 0, never 2+. Did not re-run 'event-ended' live myself -- it is the same code path with only isFinished's boolean flipped (already exercised by the pure-function unit tests, and already independently live-verified by REVIEWER's re-gate for this exact branch); re-running an identical code path a third time adds no new evidence. docker compose torn down with `docker compose down -v` and the scratch script deleted; `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean before writing this verdict. 3. S11 (PII-in-payload) re-verified directly against the live rows above, not by reading the code: both captured rows have a payload with exactly one key, `reason`, one of the three fixed enum literals -- no free text, no tg_username, no tg_id, no phone/email. entityId is the event's internal uuid (matches checkin.ts's own pre-existing 'not-found before authorization' precedent that event ids are not secret). actorUserId is either null or the resolved internal users.id -- never a Telegram id. This closes the original S5 finding without opening any new S11 exposure. 4. New-concern check for the fix itself (task step 4): does writing an audit row on every refusal open a new information-disclosure or resource-exhaustion angle? Reasoned through both: (a) Information disclosure -- the row is written server-side into audit_log, which per S12/decisions is readable only by organizer/owner-gated export tooling (not touched by this diff) and is never echoed back to the caller; checkin.ts's reply is unchanged (still the single generic notAuthorized string, no branch-specific text), so the fix creates no new oracle for an unauthorized caller to learn *why* they were refused. (b) Resource exhaustion -- an attacker spamming /checkin now causes one extra INSERT per attempt versus zero before. At PRD 1's stated load (~1,000 users, 0.06 rps peak, single Postgres, pool of 5), this is not a meaningfully new DoS surface: the attempt already required a full auth-check DB round trip (resolveActingUser + getEventStaffRow) before reaching the audit write, so the marginal cost of the fix is one more small INSERT on an already-DB-bound path, not a new unbounded amplification vector. No rate-limiting requirement is stated anywhere in security-invariants.md or the design for /checkin, so this is not a regression against any existing invariant -- noted as an observation, not a blocker. Conclusion: no new S1-S14 concern introduced by this fix. 5. Scope re-confirmed via `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-018 --name-only`: apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts + .test.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/auditLog.ts, plus the files already covered by my original full pass (domain/eventStaff.ts+test, domain/user.ts, handlers/staff.ts, handlers/checkin.ts, i18n/en.ts+ru.ts+types.ts, index.ts, docs/agents/design/REQ-018.md) and handoff bookkeeping under handoffs/WF02-REQ-018/. No apps/web files, no schema/migration file (confirmed: apps/bot/drizzle/ contains only the same 4 .sql files that existed before this rework, `git diff master...feature/WF02-REQ-018 -- apps/bot/drizzle/` is empty) -- S13 migration sign-off duty is NOT triggered by this diff. 6. Commands run myself, real output: `npm run lint` -- 0 errors (2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings, unrelated to this diff, unchanged); `npm run build` (both workspaces) -- Next.js build compiled successfully, `tsc -p tsconfig.json` for apps/bot clean; `npx vitest run` -- 10 files / 118 tests passed, matching the count both BACKEND-DEV and REVIEWER reported (114 + the 4 new buildCheckinRefusalAudit cases). All three run fresh, not copied from a prior report. ActorUserId widening re-checked: schema (db/schema.ts:314) has no `.notNull()` on actor_user_id -- null is a valid value at the DB level, confirmed by the successful insert in my own live run above, not just by reading the column definition. Grepped every writeAuditLog call site (domain/event.ts x4, domain/eventStaff.ts x2, domain/venue.ts x3, plus the new one in eventStaffAuthorization.ts) -- every pre-existing caller still passes a plain non-null string, so the type widening is backward compatible and `npm run build`'s clean tsc pass confirms no other call site broke. All applicable S1-S14 items from my original pass stand unchanged (this rework touches only the S5 gap); S5 now PASSES.
